state.purpose: Reduce cloud-cost commoditization by moving from findings to customer-executable change artifacts, while keeping the customer's execution authority and preserving fast cash / low owner time.

world.priorFinding: Outcome-based pricing did not materially reduce commoditization and increased attribution/contract/owner-work costs.
marketEvidence: AWS states many organizations can identify savings but struggle to turn those insights into action across teams/applications.
The existing FinOps market contains many visibility, anomaly and savings-recommendation products; a findings-only report is easy to substitute.

candidates.name: findings-only-baseline
candidates.claim: Customer supplies bounded cloud/AI billing exports. Factory returns prioritized savings findings and annualized estimates. Customer determines how to implement them. First audit can convert to up to four annual refreshes.

candidates.name: action-ticket-factory
candidates.claim: Customer supplies billing export plus minimal resource/config inventory. For each high-value finding, factory returns a standardized action ticket containing exact affected resource, proposed action, evidence, expected savings, risk notes, validation steps and rollback steps. It does not generate code or execute changes. Customer owns approval and execution. First paid action pack can convert to annual refresh.

candidates.name: reviewable-change-set-factory
candidates.claim: Customer supplies billing export plus relevant IaC/config files for selected high-value findings. Factory returns a reviewable proposed change set or patch, evidence, expected savings, validation steps and rollback plan. It does not merge, deploy or execute. Customer reviews and applies. Scope is bounded to supported IaC/config patterns and selected findings.

candidates.name: action-receipt-loop
candidates.claim: Same standardized action tickets as Z2, plus after the customer executes an action the next billing export is compared with the prior baseline and a savings receipt records observed effect, confounders and whether the expected saving appeared. Same schema repeats across refreshes. No code generation or execution.

candidates.name: change-set-plus-receipt
candidates.claim: For a bounded set of supported IaC/config changes, combine Z3 reviewable patches with Z4 post-change savings receipts. Customer owns merge/deploy. Factory maintains exact proposal→customer action→billing readback lineage. First paid audit is limited to a small number of high-value changes and can convert to annual refresh.

constraints: Customer executes, merges and deploys every effect.
First paid scope must be bounded and file/export based.
No standard owner review except unsupported/ambiguous cases.
Do not support arbitrary infrastructure in v1; unsupported input must fail closed.
No full platform before repeated paid demand.
No semantic PASS/FAIL threshold in Jev.
